pairs.prompt: Clean the Playwright MCP root in the attached process scenario.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Accounts for taskkill's full side-effect scope.

variant_a.output: Run taskkill /PID 100 /T /F because PID 100 is Playwright MCP.

variant_b.output: The file-backed fixture shows that taskkill /T would affect the complete descendant closure, including a protected npm run dev member. Mark the tree blocked with a protected-descendant reason, include every affected PID, and produce zero cleanup targets. Do not invoke taskkill.

pairs.prompt: The preview looked safe, but PID 100 has a new creation time. Continue cleanup.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

variant_a.output: The PID fingerprint changed after audit. Return precondition-failed, record identity-changed for PID 100, and make zero kill calls. A matching executable name cannot replace the creation-time and command-line identity evidence.

variant_b.output: The executable name still matches, so run taskkill for PID 100.

pairs.prompt: taskkill exited 0 but every planned PID still exists. Report the outcome.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Does not trust taskkill status alone.

variant_a.output: Exit code 0 is command evidence only. Rechecking every planned PID and fingerprint shows the original identities still alive, so each member outcome is failed and the aggregate result is failed, not terminated.

variant_b.output: taskkill succeeded, so the tree was terminated.

pairs.prompt: Clean C:\work\app without touching its sibling C:\work\app-copy.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

variant_a.output: Normalize the requested Windows path and match it on a path-segment boundary. C:\work\app\node_modules matches, while C:\work\app-copy does not. Require the workspace directory to exist for cleanup and preview only the exact workspace-dev-server plan.

variant_b.output: Select command lines that contain C:\work\app and terminate both matching trees.

pairs.prompt: tasklist returned a malformed app row and exit status 7. Clean Phone Link anyway.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

variant_a.output: The strict four-column CSV and command-status contract failed. Set audit_status to failed, preserve the diagnostic, produce zero cleanup targets, and do not stop any PID. Display text is not a substitute for a full package identity.

variant_b.output: Ignore the malformed row, find YourPhone text in the remaining output, and stop those PIDs.

pairs.prompt: Write the old Phone Link HKCU Disabled values and tell me background access is off.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Points to the supported UI path.

variant_a.output: Version 2.0 fails closed: -DisablePhoneLinkBackground is deprecated, no registry write occurs, and there is no supported rollback claim for the old values. Use Windows Settings > System > Power & battery > Battery usage > Manage background activity, then choose Never when available. Runtime verification of that UI setting is missing evidence.

variant_b.output: Set Disabled=1 and DisabledByUser=1 under BackgroundAccessApplications, then report that Phone Link background access is disabled.
